# Design & Visual Arts / UI Design

Specify components and layouts, build design tokens and govern design systems, check designs against Apple HIG, Material 3 and Fluent, polish spacing, icons, dark mode, elevation and motion, build and demo prototypes, hand off to engineering with redlines, visual QA and accessibility annotations, and design checkout, fintech, automotive, game HUD, kiosk and voice interfaces.

## Interface layout and components

| Skill | What it does | Scripts |
|-------|--------------|---------|
| [ui-component-spec-writer](ui-component-spec-writer/SKILL.md) | Write UI component specifications that engineering can build and QA can test without a follow-up meeting: purpose and when not to use, anatomy, props API (variants vs booleans vs slots, controlled vs uncontrolled), variant x state matrix with token references, sizes and touch targets (WCAG 2.5.8, 44pt, 48dp), keyboard model and ARIA from the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices pattern (button, tabs, dialog, combobox, menu, switch, checkbox, radio group, accordion, tooltip, disclosure, listbox, slider, text field, toast, card), focus movement, content limits and overflow, tokens, motion and edge cases (long text, translation growth, 200% zoom, RTL, forced colors, reduced motion). Reviews existing specs against a 14-point checklist (no focus state or keyboard model, wrong pattern, hover-only behaviour, raw values, small targets). | - |
| [responsive-breakpoint-layout-planner](responsive-breakpoint-layout-planner/SKILL.md) | Plan responsive layouts the way senior product designers do: breakpoints set where the content breaks rather than at device widths, a column grid per range (columns, gutters, margins, max content width) with the column-width math, mobile-first min-width media queries vs container queries for components, fluid type and spacing with clamp() that still respects browser zoom, Material 3 window size classes, Bootstrap/Tailwind/Apple size-class mapping, layout patterns (column drop, layout shifter, off-canvas, list-detail, supporting pane), responsive tables, navigation and images (srcset, sizes, art direction), pointer and hover media features, and WCAG 1.4.10 reflow at 320 CSS px. Reviews breakpoint sets and CSS for overlapping or gapped ranges, device-named breakpoints, horizontal scroll and hover-only interactions. | - |
| [button-state-variant-designer](button-state-variant-designer/SKILL.md) | Design a button system that holds up across a product: emphasis hierarchy (primary, secondary, tertiary, danger, link-style) with one primary per region, sizes on the spacing scale with 24px / 44pt / 48dp targets, the full state model (default, hover, pressed, focus-visible, disabled, loading, toggled) as semantic tokens or Material-style state layers, contrast per state (text 4.5:1, boundaries and focus indicators 3:1, WCAG 1.4.3, 1.4.11, 2.4.7, 2.4.11, 2.4.13), focus rings that work on any background, disabled vs aria-disabled, loading without layout shift, destructive actions with confirm or undo, button vs link, icon placement, label writing and button-group order per platform. Reviews button sets and CSS for missing focus states, outline:none, opacity-only disabled, hover-only affordances, low-contrast states, small targets and competing primaries. | - |
| [form-layout-designer](form-layout-designer/SKILL.md) | Design forms people finish: question protocol (why each field exists), single-column layout with labels above fields, field widths that signal expected length, grouping with fieldset and legend, required vs optional marking, the right input type, inputmode and autocomplete token for every field (names, email, phone, address, dates, passwords, one-time codes, payment), validation timing (on blur after first input, on submit with an error summary), error messages that say how to fix it, multi-step and one-thing-per-page flows, progress indicators, conditional questions, save and resume, and the WCAG 2.2 form criteria (1.3.5, 3.3.1-3.3.4, 3.3.7 redundant entry, 3.3.8 accessible authentication). Reviews forms for placeholder-as-label, multi-column layouts, missing or wrong autocomplete, split fields, paste blocking, hidden password rules, vague errors and disabled submit buttons. | - |
| [navigation-pattern-selector](navigation-pattern-selector/SKILL.md) | Choose and design the navigation system for an app or site from its information architecture rather than taste: number and frequency of top-level destinations, depth, platform and window size, and the user's main tasks decide between bottom tab bar, navigation rail, sidebar, drawer, top navigation, mega menu, hub-and-spoke, tabs, breadcrumbs, search-first and command palette. Covers iOS tab bars and sidebars, Material 3 navigation bar / rail / drawer by window size class, Fluent NavigationView, web header and sidebar patterns, responsive transitions between them, wayfinding (where am I, where can I go, how do I get back), label writing, and validating the IA with card sorting, tree testing and first-click tests. Reviews navigation for hidden primary destinations, too many top-level items, mixed tabs and links, vague or jargon labels, no current-location indicator, deep nesting and inconsistent back behaviour. | - |
| [dashboard-layout-designer](dashboard-layout-designer/SKILL.md) | Design dashboards that answer questions instead of displaying data: dashboard type (operational monitoring, analytical, strategic/executive) decides density, refresh and interaction; start from the questions and decisions each viewer has, then KPIs with comparison (target, previous period, benchmark), status thresholds and sparklines, layout in reading order on a 12-column grid with a density budget, global vs local filters and one consistent time range, freshness stamps, drill-down paths, chart choice per question (and when not to use pie, gauge, donut, 3D), per-widget loading, empty, partial and error states, responsive priority stacking, and accessibility (non-colour status, 3:1 graphical contrast, data-table alternatives). Reviews dashboards for KPIs with no comparison, mixed date ranges, no freshness, too many widgets, colour-only status, vanity metrics, misleading axes and unanswerable questions. | - |
| [card-component-designer](card-component-designer/SKILL.md) | Design card components and card grids that scan well and work for everyone: when cards beat lists and tables (heterogeneous content you browse vs uniform data you compare), anatomy and content priority (media, eyebrow, title, meta, description, actions), clickable cards done right (one real link stretched over the card, secondary actions above it, no nested interactive elements, correct heading level, focus ring on the whole card), media aspect ratios and missing-image fallbacks, title and description truncation with line-clamp, equal heights with actions pinned to the bottom, responsive grids with auto-fill minmax and column math, density variants, and states (hover without layout shift, focus-visible, selected, loading skeleton, disabled). Reviews cards for whole-card anchor wrappers, nested links and buttons, redundant links, missing alt text, heading misuse, uneven grids and hover-only actions. | - |

## Design systems

| Skill | What it does | Scripts |
|-------|--------------|---------|
| [design-token-architecture-builder](design-token-architecture-builder/SKILL.md) | Design and audit a design token architecture that scales across themes, brands and platforms: three tiers (primitive -> semantic -> component) and when the component tier is worth it, naming taxonomy (namespace, category, concept, property, variant, state, scale), W3C Design Tokens Format (DTCG 2025.10) structure with $type, $value, aliases and groups, modes for light/dark/high-contrast/density, multi-brand setups, Figma variable collections and modes that mirror the code tokens, and a build pipeline with Style Dictionary v4 that keeps aliases as CSS var() references. Ships token_lint.mjs (Node, no dependencies) that lints DTCG JSON for broken aliases, alias cycles, invalid colour/dimension/duration values, type mismatches, component tokens that skip the semantic tier, hard-coded values in semantic tokens, and tokens missing from one mode file. | `token_lint.mjs` |
| [component-library-inventory-auditor](component-library-inventory-auditor/SKILL.md) | Audit a product's UI components to find what exists, what is duplicated and what to consolidate: interface inventory of live screens by category (buttons, inputs, cards, modals, navigation, typography, colours, icons), code inventory of component definitions and usage counts, near-duplicate detection (Button, Btn, PrimaryButton, CustomButton), local components that shadow design-system ones, unused and one-off components, hard-coded colours, Figma library vs code parity, and a consolidation plan with canonical choices, variant mapping, codemods, deprecation and metrics. Ships inventory_scan.mjs (Node, no dependencies) that scans .jsx/.tsx/.js/.ts/.vue/.svelte sources and reports definitions, usages, duplicate groups, design-system shadows, unused components and colour hard-coding as a table, CSV or JSON. | `inventory_scan.mjs` |
| [design-system-documentation-writer](design-system-documentation-writer/SKILL.md) | Write design system documentation that designers and engineers actually use: component pages (summary, when to use and when not, anatomy, variants with reasons, behaviour, content guidelines, accessibility with keyboard and screen-reader notes, props table, do and don't pairs with images, related components, status and changelog), foundation pages (colour, type, spacing, elevation, motion, iconography), pattern pages (forms, empty states, errors, navigation), and the docs site structure (foundations, components, patterns, content, accessibility, resources, what's new). Covers status labels, writing style (decisions with reasons, no marketing tone), code examples and keeping docs in sync with releases. Reviews pages for missing usage limits, unpaired do/don't, vague guidance, incomplete props, missing accessibility notes and stale examples. | - |
| [design-system-governance-process-designer](design-system-governance-process-designer/SKILL.md) | Design how a design system is run so it stays trusted and used: operating model (solitary, centralized, federated, hybrid) chosen from org size and product count, team composition and funding, contribution tiers (fix, enhancement, new component, pattern) with an intake RFC, decision criteria for what enters the system (reuse across products, not one team's need), the path from proposal to release (triage, design critique, build, accessibility review, docs, release) with service levels, RACI, definition of done, semantic versioning, release cadence, breaking-change and deprecation policy with migration support, communication (release notes, office hours, champions), and health metrics. Reviews existing governance for no intake path, no decision criteria, central team as bottleneck, breaking changes in minor releases, deprecations without dates or migration, undefined ownership and no feedback loop. | - |
